text:
Alex: Heads-up — want to run a full soak + spike validation in staging for the new rate-limit enforcement changes (per-org + per-key + burst token support). Goal: validate 429 behavior, telemetry tags, and ensure our fallback routing doesn't get overloaded. Can we schedule a 2h window tonight?
Maria: +1. Which test harness are we using? k6 or the older loadtester? Also need to confirm staging quotas mirror prod configs.
Tim: Use k6 for the long soak, loadtester for tight spike tests. Staging configs were synced this morning: org_rate_limit=2000rpm, key_rate_limit=500rpm, burst_tokens=200. I pushed a config PR to infra: https://git.internal/repo/infra/PR/482
Sasha: Important: tag every request with org_id and api_key in the span so metrics/alerts can be filtered. Also add route_name and model_variant so we can see fallback churn.
Alex: Agreed. Also let's measure KV cache hit-rate and batching efficiency under quota pressure.
Tim: Sample k6 invocation for baseline soak (2h):
```
k6 run --duration 2h --vus 250 soak-k6.js --out influxdb=http://influx.staging:8086
```
And the core loop in soak-k6.js is just POST /v1/generate with varying prompt lengths and random api_key/org_id headers.
Maria: For spikes, we'll do short bursts: 2000 VUs for 30s pointed at a single key to verify per-key throttling triggers 429 fast, and then verify global org fallbacks after per-key saturates.
loadbot: spike test queued: job-id=stg-spike-174350
deploy-bot: Canaries up: rate-limiter-v2 deployed to staging cluster a and b at 1743507800
Jordan: When tests hit 429s we need logs that include: request_id, org_id, api_key_hash, route, limiter_bucket_state. Otherwise SRE won't be able to debug.
Sasha: Put a structured field limiter_state: {"tokens":X,"last_refill":T} in logs. We can redact api_key but include hash.
Tim: Example curl to replay a failing request (use staging API key):
```
curl -i -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer stg-key-XXXX" \ 
  -H "X-Org-ID: org_test_42" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}'
```
Maria: After the soak, collect these metrics: 429_count by org/key, pct_50/95/99 latency by route, KV cache hit ratio, batch size distribution, and kube pod CPU/mem. Also export per-key token bucket refill traces.
Alex: Can we add a temporary dashboard in Grafana that aggregates 429s by org and shows a heatmap over time? Put alerts: if a single org has >5% of requests 429 for >5m, notify #incidents-staging.
Sasha: I'll add a dashboard panel and an alert rule. Also we should wire a short-lived alert for high fallback rate to cheaper model variants — want to catch noisy degradations.
Tim: Ran a quick smoke locally: when a single key gets hammered, limiter returns 429 and X-RateLimit-Remaining goes to 0 as expected. But noticed 1% of 429s lacked request_id — that's a logging race when we short-circuit. Fixing now.
Alex: Good catch. Prioritize the request_id fix before the long soak.
Maria: Scheduling: start at 23:00 UTC, run 2h soak + two 1m spikes at T+30m and T+90m. I'll coordinate with QA and SRE.
Jordan: Add a post-test checklist: attach raw pprof CPU profiles, node exporter data, and a snapshot of limiter config. We should also export the k6 summaries and raw response samples.
loadbot: soak test started: job=stg-soak-1743506789, start=1743508800
Tim: Early results after 15m: overall 429_rate ~0.7%, single-key spike 429_rate ~82% during spikes, org-level 429 remained <3% after fallback routing distribution. KV hit-rate dropped by 12% under sustained pressure.
Sasha: Noted — KV drop could increase cost. Add caching warmup in the soak next time.
Alex: After finishing, prepare a brief runbook: acceptance criteria
- No more than 1% 429s for healthy orgs during soak
- Spikes should trigger per-key 429s quickly and not collapse entire org
- Telemetry must show org_id + api_key_hash on 100% of 429s
- Dashboards and alerts firing as configured
Maria: If we fail any criteria, rollback limiter config to previous version and throttle traffic to dedicated canary nodes.
Tim: Results to collect: grafana dashboard link, k6 summary, k6 raw CSV, code change PRs, and a short incident ticket if thresholds exceeded.
Alex: Thanks all — @Sasha please create the dashboard and alert, @Maria coordinate the window, @Tim and @Jordan make sure logs and traces are intact. I'll monitor the soak and jump in if anything looks bad. :thumbsup:
Maria: A few follow-ups: add a synthetic client id rotation to the soak so we don't hit key exhaustion unrealistically, and include a low-qps control group to compare.
Sasha: Dashboard created: https://grafana.staging/d/abc123/rate-limiter-soak (temp). Alert rule pushed.
loadbot: soak finished: job=stg-soak-1743506789, end=1743510300, summary: total_reqs=3,456,789, 429_total=34,512 (0.998%), top_orgs_with_429=[org_test_42:12,345, org_big_7:8,999]
Tim: I'll open a short postmortem if any criteria are missed. Early glance: looks within acceptance but need to review tail latency.
Alex: Perfect. If everyone is happy, we'll promote the config to canary in prod next week with a smaller traffic % and repeat a shorter soak there. Thanks!
